link-rebaser-deterministic-text-cleanup-.rule: Deterministic text-cleanup transforms over rule/doc prose that embeds code samples MUST be deletion-only — never reflow whitespace or punctuation. A cosmetic `replace(/\s+([,.;:])/g, '$1')` or multi-space collapse corrupts embedded code: `${{ ... }}` → `${{... }}`, `exit 1 ;;` → `exit 1;;`, `[ref]: ...` → `[ref]:...`. To strip a trailing marker that owns its terminal period, make the period part of the marker's own regex match (e.g. `\bSee\s+L\d+\.?`) instead of post-collapsing `..` afterward. Verify any prose transform against the real corpus and assert ellipses/fences/shell-punctuation survive byte-for-byte.

link-rebaser-never-leave-a-scratch-deliv.rule: Never leave a scratch/delivery file at the repo root whose basename matches a canonical artifact (e.g. lessons.json): the reference rewriter is project-root-relative and existence-gated, so 'agentsmesh generate' resolves canonical paths like .agentsmesh/lessons/lessons.json down to the root lessons.json and silently rewrites every generated root-instruction file (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .goosehints, ...). Use a non-colliding name (lessons.fixed.json) or write outside the repo, then re-run generate.

link-rebaser-rule-1.rule: Treat reference-style Markdown definitions (`[ref]: ...`, titled, angle-bracketed) as link destinations, not prose anchors — apply the same destination-relative rewrite contract as inline links.

link-rebaser-rule-10.rule: Preserve/add `./` prefix for same-directory descendant links inside generated Markdown (`formatLinkPathForDestination`). Assert the exact rendered path (`./skills/post-feature-qa/`) in tests, never "not canonical" loose matches.

link-rebaser-rule-11.rule: URI-skip patterns (`ssh://`, `git@host:`) must keep the scheme matcher distinct from Windows drive-letter detection — never let a single-letter scheme regex swallow `C:` and block legitimate absolute paths. Add same-file regression for both.

link-rebaser-rule-12.rule: Path tokenizers must require enough structure to distinguish file references from prose markers — the absolute-path branch must NOT match a bare `/` (e.g. `✓ / ✗` status text).

link-rebaser-rule-13.rule: Inline backtick path rewrites: tests asserting the rewritten form must accept any of `` `docs/...` ``, `` `/docs/...` ``, `` `./docs/...` ``, `` `../docs/...` `` via a permissive regex — Windows 8.3-shortname realpath divergence makes the exact form non-deterministic. The contract is "stable destination," not "always project-root-relative."

link-rebaser-rule-14.rule: `expandResolvedPaths` must yield the caller's `projectRoot`-shaped path FIRST, then the realpath variant as a tie-breaker — never `unshift(realPath)`. Realpath-first breaks `toProjectRootRelative` on DOS short names (`RUNNER~1` vs `runneradmin`) and symlinked tmpdirs. Audit every `[realpath, original]` loop.

link-rebaser-rule-15.rule: Import normalization must include BOTH the direct joined target path AND its `realpathSync.native` variant in the lookup map. Temp-workspace runs resolve through realpath and otherwise stay target-specific after import.

link-rebaser-rule-16.rule: Import normalization must build the rewrite map from every supported generated path family across ALL targets, not just the source target — re-importing a polluted artifact must recover canonical `.agentsmesh/...` links cross-family.

link-rebaser-rule-17.rule: Do not normalize bare root filenames (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `GEMINI.md`) as raw substrings on the import side — they are common standalone words in prose. Only normalize when they appear in a structured path form.

link-rebaser-rule-18.rule: Any code participating in the link-rewrite map (key construction OR lookup) MUST use `pathApi(projectRoot)` from `src/core/path-helpers.ts`. NEVER import `join`/`normalize` from `node:path` directly in `src/core/reference/` or target-side `applyXxxRefs` helpers.

link-rebaser-rule-19.rule: Unit tests using a synthetic POSIX root (e.g. `ROOT = '/proj'`) with link-rewrite map machinery must alias `join`/`normalize` to `posix.join`/`posix.normalize` from `node:path/posix` — host `node:path` is win32 on Windows runners and silently mismatches the map.

link-rebaser-rule-2.rule: Preserve well-known canonical tokens (e.g. `.agentsmesh/`) in prose/labels/quoted/reading-context positions, but rewrite real Markdown inline-link destinations cross-format. Audit prose vs link classifier whenever formatter semantics change.

link-rebaser-rule-20.rule: After extracting helpers from `link-rebaser.ts` (e.g. `normalizeSeparators`, formatter helpers), scan every remaining branch (especially preservation/protected paths) for moved symbols and rerun the narrowest affected suite BEFORE expanding verification.

link-rebaser-rule-21.rule: Whenever the link-rewriter protection contract changes (fenced code, inline backticks, URI skips, drive letters), update both the main rewrite tests AND `link-rebaser-edge-cases.test.ts` in the same pass — the edge-case suite codifies the same contract separately.

link-rebaser-rule-22.rule: Reference-rewrite audits must search REAL canonical content for path patterns (including directory-form refs like `.agentsmesh/skills/post-feature-qa/`) and add tests for both exact files AND directory-form references. Synthetic round trips are insufficient — regenerate live target artifacts and grep the exact reported pattern.

link-rebaser-rule-23.rule: Generated Markdown demo content must use link destinations that resolve from EVERY generated target folder after rebasing. Keep speculative project-root examples as prose, not as clickable Markdown destinations.

link-rebaser-rule-24.rule: When parsing inline-link destinations with regex captures (e.g. `parseMarkdownLinkDestination`), guard the specific capture explicitly (`match?.[1] !== undefined`) under strict indexed access — don't rely on regex structure.

link-rebaser-rule-25.rule: Before adding extension-level skip gates in `rewriteGeneratedReferences()`, inspect the reference-rewrite matrix — supporting files like `template.ts` comments must still be rewritten; only token/comment-aware logic, not a blanket non-Markdown skip.

link-rebaser-rule-26.rule: Strict-prose assertions ("no leftover canonical mesh path") must run on prose with ALL rewriter-protected tokens stripped (fenced code, external refs, AND Windows absolute path tokens `/[A-Za-z]:[\\/][^\s,<>"'+'`'+`]+/`). The `WINDOWS_ABSOLUTE_PATH` guard in `link-rebaser.ts` is by-design.

link-rebaser-rule-27.rule: `shouldRewritePathToken` must split quote-like wrappers by intent: backticks (`` ` ``) are inline code and rewrite; single (`'`) and double (`"`) quotes are string-literal contexts inside code-like prose and stay verbatim. Don't restore the three-wrapper conflation in `link-token-context.ts`. When a canonical script needs a sibling file, author `Path(__file__).parent / "sibling.py"`, not `Path(__file__).parent / ".agentsmesh/skills/.../sibling.py"` — relying on the rebaser to "fix" the latter is the masking pattern this rule retires.

link-rebaser-rule-3.rule: Never inline `.agentsmesh/` as an exact substring in generated root-instruction decoration prose — reference-rewrite e2e strips fenced code and asserts the substring is gone. Phrase as ``the `.agentsmesh` directory at the project root``. Strip both old and new contract blocks on import.

link-rebaser-rule-4.rule: Add every emitted artifact path (including `additionalRootDecorationPaths`, multi-output families like Copilot's `.github/copilot/*.instructions.md` + `.github/instructions/*.md`, and Windsurf shared `AGENTS.md`) to the generate-side output-source map and build rewrite maps per output path / artifact family, not just per target.

link-rebaser-rule-5.rule: Pack skill artifact paths (`.agentsmesh/packs/.../skills/...`) must be added to `buildArtifactPathMap` alongside canonical `.agentsmesh/skills/...` so the rebaser translates both canonical and pack absolute paths.

link-rebaser-rule-6.rule: Shared artifact collision must compare canonicalized (un-rewritten) content, not post-rewrite bytes — collapse target-specific rewritten links back to canonical before declaring a true conflict. Keep target-native rewrite probes in protected fenced blocks or target-filtered fixtures so they don't poison shared outputs.

link-rebaser-rule-7.rule: Existence-gate rewriting: classify "should rewrite" vs "should stay unchanged because resolution fails" explicitly. Don't blindly normalize relative-looking refs whose targets don't exist (e.g. missing checklist refs, fixture `../SKILL.md`). Audit both categories whenever the link contract changes.

link-rebaser-rule-8.rule: For bare multi-segment paths under a root-relative contract (`src/AGENTS.md`, `docs/...`), resolve from the project root first, fall back to source-relative only if the root candidate is invalid. Add nested-file regression tests.

link-rebaser-rule-9.rule: For `../` over-traversal that escapes the workspace, retry resolution from the project root before giving up — real canonical files contain `../../../../docs/...` that still mean repo-root files. Cover in unit + all-target generate/import matrices.

mcp-generate-lock-the-mcp-generate-handl.rationale: MCP generate wrote target files but not .agentsmesh/.lock while returning lockfileUpdated:true; routing through runGenerate fixed it.
mcp-generate-lock-the-mcp-generate-handl.rule: The MCP generate handler (src/mcp/handlers/orchestrate.ts) MUST delegate to the CLI runGenerate, never reimplement file-writing — a bespoke reimplementation silently skips the lockfile write, stale-output cleanup, and process lock that `agentsmesh generate` guarantees, leaving `check` permanently drifted.

pnpm-lockfile-in-this-repo-run-dev.rule: In this repo, run dev tooling via `node_modules/.bin/<tool>` (vitest, tsup, tsx, changeset) — NOT `pnpm <script>` / `pnpm exec`. Any pnpm-11 invocation runs a deps-status-check that strips the pnpm-10 `hono` override from `pnpm-lock.yaml`, re-breaking CI's `--frozen-lockfile`. After build/test/changeset runs, check `git status`; if `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.agentsmesh/.lock` (timestamp-only), or `tests/e2e/agents-last-run.md` show as modified, `git checkout -- <them>` before committing — they are spurious churn.

pnpm-lockfile-the-committed-pnpm-lock-ya.rationale: CI frozen install failed because package.json's hono override was missing from the lockfile; local pnpm 11 reported the lockfile up-to-date and would not add it, so the fix required regenerating with pnpm 10.
pnpm-lockfile-the-committed-pnpm-lock-ya.rule: The committed `pnpm-lock.yaml` `overrides:` block must match `package.json` `pnpm.overrides` exactly, or CI's `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails with ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH. CI runs pnpm 10 (pinned via `pnpm/action-setup` `version: 10`); local pnpm 11 will NOT repair the mismatch — `pnpm install --lockfile-only` reports "Already up to date" and leaves the overrides snapshot stale. Regenerate with the CI major and verify with it: `CI=true npx -y pnpm@10 install --lockfile-only` then `CI=true npx -y pnpm@10 install --frozen-lockfile` must exit 0 before committing.

process-locks-when-wiring-any-process-lo.rule: When wiring any process lock through acquireProcessLock (a new *-lock.ts wrapper or an inline call), pass a human-readable label (e.g. 'lessons lock', 'install lock') in LockOptions — LockAcquisitionError builds its message from that label and silently defaults to a generic 'lock', so a forgotten label mislabels the lock in the contention error without failing any test.

When wiring any process lock through acquireProcessLock (a new *-lock.ts wrapper or an inline call), pass a human-readable label (e.g. 'lessons lock', 'install lock') in LockOptions — LockAcquisitionError builds its message from that label and silently defaults to a generic 'lock', so a forgotten label mislabels the lock in the contention error without failing any test.

readme-authoring-when-trimming-or-rewrit.rationale: User correction: a lean rewrite dropped the init wizard and auto link rebasing; the user had to ask for a deep feature re-check and a second rewrite.
readme-authoring-when-trimming-or-rewrit.rule: When trimming or rewriting README.md, do not sacrifice feature coverage for brevity. Cross-check the rewrite against the actual feature set (website/src/content/docs/** and src/cli/help-data.ts) and keep the differentiators — especially the `init` interactive wizard (targets → import → lessons → generate) and automatic link rebasing (canonical refs like `.agentsmesh/skills/.../x` rewritten to each target's native path). The readme skill's "lean" default must not silently drop recently-added or distinguishing features.

readme-codegen-blocks-when-trimming-or-r.rationale: A README cleanup can delete the wide matrix tables as "clutter", which breaks matrix:generate (throws on missing markers) and matrix-docs.test.ts (pins the first |Feature| table + exact global-scope heading).
readme-codegen-blocks-when-trimming-or-r.rule: When trimming or rewriting README.md, preserve the auto-generated marker blocks `<!-- agentsmesh:support-matrix:project -->`, `<!-- agentsmesh:support-matrix:global -->`, and `<!-- agentsmesh:tool-list -->`; keep the exact heading `### Global scope (`agentsmesh generate --global`)` directly above the global matrix; and keep the project matrix as the FIRST `| Feature ` table (give other tables a different first column, e.g. `| Command |`). `scripts/render-support-matrix.ts` throws on missing matrix markers and `tests/unit/core/matrix-docs.test.ts` pins this layout — finish with `pnpm matrix:generate && pnpm matrix:verify`.

release-changesets-when-auditing-which-c.rationale: A release audit found a feat(skills) commit that needed no changeset (repo-internal only) and an unlabeled MCP bug fix that did — classification hinges on the npm files surface.
release-changesets-when-auditing-which-c.rule: When auditing which changes since the last release tag need a changeset, only the npm-published surface is user-facing: `src/`, `schemas/`, `package.json` (deps/exports), and `README.md` (the package `files` field is dist/schemas/README.md/CHANGELOG.md/LICENSE). Changes confined to `.agentsmesh/`, `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `tests/`, `website/`, or `docs/` ship nothing and need NO changeset — even a `feat(...)`-prefixed commit (e.g. adding a repo-internal skill). Enumerate with `git log v<last-tag>..HEAD --no-merges` and map every user-facing commit to a changeset.

security-a-directory-reader-that-ingests.rule: A directory reader that ingests untrusted native/pack content into canonical or a redistributable pack must not follow escaping symlinks; when hardening one reader (e.g. the canonical rules/commands/agents parsers), fix EVERY sibling reader — the native import readers (import-orchestrator, skill-import-pipeline, target-native-commands, per-target importers) share the exact same exfiltration class, so half-fixing leaves host-secret exfiltration open. For untrusted git clones also set core.symlinks=false.

security-when-hardening-a-git-spawn.rule: When hardening a git spawn site against SSRF/redirect (assertAllowedGitUrl + GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL), apply the SAME guard to ALL git spawn runners — the clone runner in src/config/remote/git-remote.ts, not just ls-remote in src/install/source/git-pin.ts. String-level parseGitSource validation does not constrain server-side redirects during clone.

security-when-hardening-git-transport-se.rule: When hardening git transport security, apply the protocol allowlist (assertAllowedGitUrl) AND GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL to BOTH spawn sites — the ls-remote/ref-resolution runner (git-pin.ts) and the clone runner (git-remote.ts) — and set core.symlinks=false on clone; hardening only ls-remote leaves redirect-during-clone (https->ext:: RCE, file:// read) reachable.

shell-quoting-construct-control-characte.rule: Construct control-character values directly in inline Node probes; do not interpolate raw control bytes into a JSON string and JSON.parse it, because raw line/control characters make the probe fail before testing the product.

shell-quoting-for-inline-typescript-eval.rule: For inline TypeScript eval scripts that need await, wrap the body in an async IIFE unless the runner is explicitly configured for ESM output.

shell-quoting-never-insert-zero-width-or.rationale: A zero-width space used to avoid closing a JSDoc block comment failed pnpm lint (no-irregular-whitespace).
shell-quoting-never-insert-zero-width-or.rule: Never insert zero-width or other irregular whitespace (e.g. U+200B) into source to dodge an accidental `*/` block-comment close — ESLint `no-irregular-whitespace` fails the lint gate. Reword the prose so the literal `*/` fence never appears (drop the inline example or describe it), rather than hiding a control byte in the comment.

shell-quoting-rule-1.rule: For inline Node scripts that use top-level `await`, use ESM `import` syntax; otherwise wrap CommonJS `require` code in an async IIFE. Never mix `require` with top-level `await` in the same heredoc — Node 24 emits `ERR_AMBIGUOUS_MODULE_SYNTAX`.

shell-quoting-rule-10.rule: Installer scripts that auto-edit shell rc files must key BOTH the rc file path AND the line syntax off the shell name. `export PATH=...` is bash/POSIX-only — fish rejects it. For fish, use `fish_add_path -gP "$BIN_DIR"` (or `set -gx PATH "$BIN_DIR" $PATH`). Always `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$config")"` before `>>` because `~/.config/fish/` may not exist.

shell-quoting-rule-11.rule: When parsing structured `<token>  <filename>` manifests (checksums, etc.) from shell, use `awk -v t="$TARGET" '$2==t {print $1}'` — field equality, not `grep "$NEEDLE"` substring. Substring matching silently breaks when filenames share prefixes (e.g., `agentsmesh-darwin-arm64` vs `agentsmesh-darwin-arm64.exe`).

shell-quoting-rule-12.rule: Validate env-controlled paths (e.g., `$AGENTSMESH_INSTALL`) against a strict allowlist (`*[!a-zA-Z0-9./_~\ -]*`) before interpolating into any line written to a shell-rc file. Otherwise a wrapping process can inject persistent shell code via the env var.

shell-quoting-rule-13.rule: When a build/test fails with parser errors ("Unterminated string literal", "Unexpected `<<`"), scan touched files for unresolved `<<<<<<<` merge conflict markers FIRST before deeper investigation — higher-level debugging on a syntactically invalid file is noise.

shell-quoting-rule-14.rule: When an `rg` search pattern starts with `-` (or may start with `-` after interpolation), pass it with `-e '<pattern>'` or place `--` before the pattern so ripgrep cannot parse the search text as flags.

shell-quoting-rule-2.rule: Never put escaped newlines (`\n`) inside a plain `rg` regex; ripgrep is line-oriented by default. Split into multiple literal patterns, or pass `rg -U --multiline-dotall` when a true cross-line match is required.

shell-quoting-rule-3.rule: Never assign to `status` (or other zsh read-only specials) in shell cleanup snippets — use neutral names like `rc` for captured exit codes. Verify cleanup ran when the sandbox/wrapper exits unexpectedly.

shell-quoting-rule-4.rule: For `rg` patterns containing backticks, `$`, or other shell metacharacters, use single quotes with `-F` (literal mode), or split into simpler literal patterns. Never wrap such patterns in double quotes — the shell command-substitutes the backticks before `rg` ever runs.

shell-quoting-rule-5.rule: For `execSync`/`spawnSync` calls that need shell features like `2>&1`, use `/bin/sh` (or omit `shell` and avoid shell-only syntax). Never hardcode `/bin/zsh` (missing on `ubuntu-latest`) or `/bin/bash` (not guaranteed on minimal images) unless the job explicitly installs that shell.

shell-quoting-rule-6.rule: For tests that need merged stdout+stderr cross-platform, use `spawnSync(process.execPath, [...args], { encoding: 'utf-8' })` and concatenate `result.stdout + result.stderr`. Never embed `2>&1` or hardcode any `/bin/*` once Windows is in the CI matrix.

shell-quoting-rule-7.rule: Never write a literal `*/` inside any `/* ... */` or `/** ... */` block comment — including JSDoc headers in test files. Globs like `skills/*/SKILL.md` close the comment early and produce misleading parser errors at unrelated lines. Reword to `skills/{name}/SKILL.md`, `glob: *.md`, or move into a `//` single-line comment.

shell-quoting-rule-8.rule: When a TS/JS source file needs control-character escapes inside regex literals, build the regex via `new RegExp('[<>:"|?*\\u0000-\\u001F]')` or `String.fromCharCode(n)` — never put `\xNN`/`\uNNNN` directly in a `Write` tool payload, because JSON evaluates them into raw control bytes before the file is written. Verify the resulting file with `file(1)` is reported as text, not `data`.

shell-quoting-rule-9.rule: When a fixture string needs literal `<<<<<<< HEAD` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` lines at module top level, either (a) inline the literal inside a CallExpression argument, or (b) build it from concatenated parts (`'<' + '<<<<<< HEAD'`) so no source line begins with seven repeated `<`/`=`/`>`. TypeScript's lexer scans for left-anchored merge-conflict markers even inside top-level template literals (TS1185).

skill-path-resolution-resolve-skill-path.rule: Resolve skill paths from the declared skill roots before reading them.
Resolve skill paths from the repository-local skill root when a listed home-directory alias is absent.

source-verification-re-open-official-doc.rule: Re-open official documentation from a fresh search result when a stale browser reference fails.

subagent-delegation-when-spawning-a-full.rule: When spawning a full-history subagent, omit agent_type/model/reasoning overrides; use a clean context if a specialized role is required.

target-capabilities-amp-s-real-amp-hooks.rule: Amp's real amp.hooks is a flat ARRAY of rule objects [{id, compatibilityDate, on:{event:'tool:pre-execute'|'tool:post-execute', tool:[...], 'input.contains':'...'}, action:{type:'send-user-message'|'redact-tool-input', message:'...'}}] read from .amp/settings.json and ~/.config/amp/settings.json; agentsmesh emits a Claude-Code-shaped OBJECT keyed by event ({event:[{matcher,hooks:[{type,command}]}]}) under amp.hooks and has NO hooks importer, so the round-trip is broken. Do not declare amp hooks 'native' — it is 'embedded' at best until the emitter matches Amp's array schema and an importer exists.

target-capabilities-copilot-has-no-globa.rationale: Global commands declared native but Copilot CLI never reads ~/.copilot/prompts; output is silently inert.
target-capabilities-copilot-has-no-globa.rule: Copilot has NO global ~/.copilot/prompts/ surface: the official ~/.copilot config-dir reference enumerates all top-level items (agents, skills, hooks, instructions, copilot-instructions.md) and lists no prompts dir; .prompt.md is a VS Code/IDE feature. Do not declare global commands:native for copilot or emit .copilot/prompts/*.prompt.md — it is a phantom (inert) path.

target-capabilities-deepagents-cli-hooks.rule: deepagents-cli hooks are NOT Claude Code format: Deep Agents Code reads hooks.json as {\"hooks\":[{\"command\":[...],\"events\":[\"session.start\",\"session.end\",\"tool.error\",...]}]} (array of command+events objects), not the PreToolUse/PostToolUse matcher object buildClaudeHooksObjectFromCanonical emits; the generator emits the wrong schema and there is no hooks importer, so hooks:native is generate-only and produces an invalid file. Emit the deepagents array schema and wire a hooks importer.

target-capabilities-deepagents-cli-targe.rule: deepagents-cli target wraps LangChain "Deep Agents Code" (libs/code/deepagents_code), which loads custom subagents from the filesystem as Markdown+YAML-frontmatter at .deepagents/agents/{name}/AGENTS.md (project) and ~/.deepagents/{agent}/agents/{name}/AGENTS.md (user); declare agents as native, not none.

target-capabilities-for-kilo-code-the-ne.rule: For kilo-code, the new-layout `.kilo/rules/*.md` files are NOT auto-loaded by Kilo Code — each must be registered under the `instructions` array in `kilo.jsonc` (only legacy `.kilocode/rules/` auto-loads). Generating standalone `.kilo/rules/<slug>.md` without writing an `instructions` entry leaves additionalRules silently inert. Also: kilo global commands/agents live at `~/.config/kilo/commands|agents` (NOT `~/.kilo/`), global skills live at `~/.kilo/skills`, and MCP belongs in `kilo.jsonc` top-level `mcp` key (not `.kilo/mcp.json` `mcpServers`).

target-capabilities-for-the-crush-target.rule: For the crush target, only emit permissions.allowed_tools in crush.json — Crush's Go Permissions struct has no denied_tools field (json:"allowed_tools" only), so generated denied_tools is silently ignored; also permissions is a real on-disk crush.json key (read from project crush.json and global ~/.config/crush/crush.json), so it must be declared native, not partial/none.

target-capabilities-when-auditing-the-an.rule: When auditing the antigravity target's permissions capability, treat the official allowlist-denylist/permissions docs (Allow/Ask/Deny, app-managed project permissions) as the source of truth; only third-party blogs claim a committable .antigravity/settings.json with antigravity.commands.alwaysAllow/alwaysDeny keys, so cap any permissions upgrade at embedded with explicit low/medium confidence rather than native.

target-capabilities-when-declaring-the-c.rule: When declaring the copilot hooks capability, use 'native' (not 'partial') for project scope: Copilot CLI auto-loads .github/hooks/*.json at startup and agentsmesh fully owns/round-trips .github/hooks/agentsmesh.json. Global hooks are also native via ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json (same JSON format).

target-capability-audits-after-changing-.rule: After changing a target's importFrom/importer logic, rebuild dist (pnpm build) BEFORE running the e2e round-trip matrix: tests/e2e/target-contract-matrix.e2e.test.ts spawns the built dist/cli.js via runCli, while tests/contract/target-contract.matrix.test.ts calls importFrom in-process. If the contract round-trip passes but the e2e round-trip fails with a missing/extra canonical file (e.g. .agentsmesh/hooks.yaml), the dist is stale — rebuild, don't chase the importer.

target-capability-audits-capability-audi.rule: Capability audits for agentsmesh are expansion-first: preserve working experimental, compatibility, and unofficial target projections; do not downgrade or remove support merely because the vendor surface is experimental or not the preferred path. Add newly available features and document limitations.

target-capability-audits-cline-has-no-gl.rule: Cline has NO global agent-definition surface: the official ~/.cline/ tree is data/settings/{providers.json,rules/,skills/}, data/teams/, data/sessions/, data/logs/, plugins/ — no agents.yaml and no agents/ dir. agents.yaml exists ONLY at project .cline/agents.yaml (single YAML file, not a .cline/agents/*.md directory). Do not declare cline globalCapabilities.agents as 'native' and do not emit global ~/.cline/agents/*.md; global agents support is effectively none.

target-capability-audits-cursor-ide-perm.rule: Cursor IDE permissions are file-based and disk-ownable via .cursor/permissions.json (project) and ~/.cursor/permissions.json (global), JSONC, top-level keys mcpAllowlist/terminalAllowlist/autoRun{allow_instructions,block_instructions} — NOT GUI-only, so 'partial'/'none' under-declares; but canonical allow/deny/ask does not round-trip losslessly (no enforceable deny/ask, allow must be split terminal-vs-MCP). The legacy importer's .cursor/settings.json permissions key is an undocumented phantom path; the real file is .cursor/permissions.json.

target-capability-audits-for-codex-cli-c.rule: For codex-cli, `.codex/instructions/<slug>.md` is NOT a surface Codex reads (config reference marks `instructions` as reserved/future-use); Codex's real additional-rule surfaces are nested `AGENTS.md`/`AGENTS.override.md` (advisory) and `.codex/rules/*.rules` (execution policy, Starlark prefix_rule). Do not treat the instructions-mirror emit as a native additionalRules surface. Also: codex MCP `.codex/config.toml` natively supports streamable-HTTP servers via `url`/`bearer_token_env_var`/`http_headers`/`env_http_headers` (not experimental), and that file is Codex's primary config — generateMcp overwriting it whole drops both HTTP servers and all non-MCP user config.

target-capability-audits-for-gemini-cli-.rule: For Gemini CLI permissions, global (User-tier ~/.gemini/policies/*.toml) is fully loaded by the policy engine and is the recommended location, but project/workspace-tier ($WORKSPACE_ROOT/.gemini/policies/*.toml) is temporarily DISABLED upstream (issue #18186, PR #20522). So gemini-cli global permissions should be 'native' while project stays 'partial'; never raise the project permissions level above partial.

target-capability-audits-for-qwen-code-g.rule: For qwen-code, global additionalRules is native, not embedded: Qwen Code auto-loads ~/.qwen/rules/**/*.md (md + optional YAML frontmatter with description/paths) globally per PR #3339 (merged 2026-04-17), mirroring project .qwen/rules/. Wire a global rules dir constant + global layout rewrite + importer-spec global source instead of embedding into ~/.qwen/QWEN.md.

target-capability-audits-for-the-continu.rule: For the Continue target, permissions live ONLY in the global ~/.continue/permissions.yaml (Continue CLI surface, top-level keys allow/ask/exclude) — there is NO project-level permissions file; raise permissions capability for global scope only, keep project permissions=none. Hooks are NOT in Continue's config.yaml schema (verified against docs/reference and config_schema.json), so hooks must stay none for both scopes.

target-capability-audits-goose-supports-.rule: Goose supports file-based tool permissions natively in GLOBAL scope only via ~/.config/goose/permission.yaml — a YAML map keyed by category (user, smart_approve) where each category has always_allow/ask_before/never_allow string lists (verified in crates/goose/src/config/permission.rs). agentsmesh owns the `user` block (allow→always_allow, deny→never_allow, ask→ask_before) and MUST merge-preserve the runtime `smart_approve` cache. There is NO project-level permission.yaml, so project permissions stays 'none'. MCP and permissions are both global-only for Goose.

Goose supports lifecycle hooks via the Open Plugin Specification v1.0.0: a `hooks/hooks.json` file inside a plugin dir at `<project>/.agents/plugins/<name>/` (project scope) and `~/.agents/plugins/<name>/` (global scope), auto-discovered at startup (released 2026-05-14). Schema: top-level `hooks` object keyed by event (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure/SessionStart/SessionEnd/UserPromptSubmit/...), each an array of `{matcher?, hooks:[{type:"command", command}]}`. This maps onto canonical Hooks (event -> HookEntry{matcher,command,type}), so hooks is UNDER-declared as 'none' for both scopes; both project and global are file-based and round-trippable. Note the plugin-dir nesting (agentsmesh must own a plugin <name> dir), unlike Claude Code's single settings hooks key.

target-capability-audits-pi-pi-agent-nat.rule: Pi (pi-agent) natively supports prompt templates as command surface: project `.pi/prompts/*.md` and global `~/.pi/agent/prompts/*.md` (non-recursive, filename = command name, YAML frontmatter `description` + `argument-hint`, `$1`/`$ARGUMENTS` substitution). Treat `commands` as a native, round-trippable file surface — do not leave it declared `none` while only projecting commands as `.pi/skills/` bundles via supportsConversion.

target-capability-audits-when-a-target-d.rationale: codex-cli declared hooks=partial yet had generateHooks + importCodexHooks + round-trip tests + managedOutputs; partial was wrong, native was correct.
target-capability-audits-when-a-target-d.rule: When a target declares a feature `partial` but already ships a REAL generator AND importer for it (a dedicated on-disk file the tool reads, round-trip tested) — not a no-op stub — the level is a mislabel: raise it to `native`. `partial` is reserved for features that have only a no-op `generateX` returning [] plus a `lint.<feature>` warning (GUI/cloud-only surfaces agentsmesh cannot write). Diagnostic: a `partial` feature with no `lint.<feature>` stub and a wired generator in `target.generators` is almost certainly mislabeled.

target-capability-audits-when-changing-a.rationale: Cursor hooks format fix (PascalCase nested -> camelCase flat) broke 9 cross-cutting test files beyond the cursor unit dir.
target-capability-audits-when-changing-a.rule: When changing a target's generated FILE FORMAT (hook event names, object shape, or top-level key — not just the path), grep the ENTIRE tests/ tree before claiming the slice done, not just tests/unit/targets/<id>/. Format changes have wide blast radius: cross-cutting fixtures and assertions live in tests/unit/core/engine.test.ts, tests/import-generate-roundtrip.test.ts, tests/integration/*-merge & generate.integration, tests/e2e/{import,generate}-capabilities, global-roundtrip-*, hooks-roundtrip, and tests/e2e/fixtures/<target>-project/. Update every one in the same TDD slice.

target-capability-audits-when-extracting.rule: When extracting capabilities to a separate file to stay under the 200-line limit, export named constants (e.g. `projectCapabilities`, `globalCapabilities`) rather than the same names as the inline variables in index.ts — this avoids name shadowing and import confusion when the old variables are removed.

target-capability-expansion-amazon-q-cli.rule: Amazon Q CLI reads rules ONLY from project .amazonq/rules/**/*.md (auto-loaded directory of multiple .md files); it has NO global rules dir on disk (open feature request aws/amazon-q-developer-cli#3451 asks for ~/.amazonq/rules, not ~/.aws/amazonq/rules). Keep amazon-q additionalRules native for PROJECT but none for GLOBAL; the ~/.aws/amazonq/ root is real only for MCP/agents.

target-capability-expansion-before-readi.rule: Before reading a target implementation, list its files or search for the symbol; do not assume split generator/importer filenames because many targets keep them in aggregate files.

target-capability-expansion-conversion-d.rule: Conversion-disable flags must suppress only conversion-derived embedded generators; once a target gains native support, conversion settings must not disable its native generator.

target-capability-expansion-do-not-combi.rule: Do not combine an expected no-match rg probe after another read command when failure capture is mandatory; run no-match-tolerant searches separately or use an explicit read-only fallback.

target-capability-expansion-for-opencode.rule: For opencode targets, additionalRules emitted to .opencode/rules/ are NOT auto-loaded by opencode (only AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md are); to make additionalRules genuinely native, the generator must also write an "instructions" array (e.g. [".opencode/rules/*.md"]) into opencode.json, otherwise the rule files are orphaned and additionalRules is over-declared as native.

target-capability-expansion-native-targe.rule: Native target agent formats that omit canonical fields must carry those fields in x-agentsmesh extension metadata, and their import mapper must explicitly translate the extensions back before fallback serialization.

target-capability-expansion-when-a-targe.rule: When a target gains support for a previously linted unsupported feature, remove or rewrite branch tests for the obsolete lint helper in the same capability slice.
When a target output family changes, update shared E2E manifest helpers and reference-matrix expectations in addition to generation assertions; these helpers may encode the old path independently.

target-capability-expansion-when-expandi.rule: When expanding a target from agent-to-skill projection to native agent files, update strict path contracts and preserve canonical-only metadata in extension frontmatter so generate-import round trips remain lossless.

target-capability-expansion-when-repo-wi.rule: When repo-wide format:check reports pre-existing drift, format only touched files and recheck that subset; do not rewrite unrelated source files.

target-deepagents-cli-deepagents-cli-glo.rule: deepagents-cli globals are per-agent: user memory is ~/.deepagents/{assistant_id}/AGENTS.md and user skills are ~/.deepagents/{assistant_id}/skills/ (NOT flat ~/.deepagents/AGENTS.md or ~/.deepagents/skills). Its hooks.json is {"hooks":[{"command":[..],"events":["session.start"]}]} loaded only from ~/.deepagents/hooks.json — NOT the Claude-Code PreToolUse/matcher object shape, and there is no project hooks surface. deepagents also has native on-disk agents dirs (.deepagents/agents/{name}/AGENTS.md project, ~/.deepagents/{agent}/agents/{name}/AGENTS.md global).

test-execution-do-not-run-pnpm-stashed.rule: Do not run pnpm-stashed node_modules/.ignored_* package binaries directly; those directories can lack dependency resolution, so repair the install or use a complete known-good tool path instead.

test-execution-set-ci-true-when-running.rule: Set CI=true when running pnpm test or vitest from non-interactive agents so pnpm will not abort a tool-managed install purge for lack of TTY.

test-execution-use-tsx-instead-of-plain.rule: Use tsx instead of plain node when probing source TypeScript modules that contain .js-relative imports; Node can load the TS entry but will not resolve sibling .js specifiers to .ts source files.

test-execution-when-the-pnpm-shim-tries.rule: When the pnpm shim tries to recreate node_modules or fails frozen-lockfile config checks during a focused test run, avoid further pnpm test invocations and run the local test binary directly until dependencies are repaired.

test-execution-with-this-vitest-setup-pn.rule: With this Vitest setup, pnpm test -- <files> does not reliably restrict execution because the package script already ends in vitest run; use pnpm exec vitest run <files> for focused tests.

typescript-contracts-after-adding-a-new-.rule: After adding a new target generator module, verify the target-local output type name before importing it; neighboring targets use different names even when the shape is identical.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-1.rule: Place every per-target `ImportEntryMapper` referenced by the descriptor object literal in a third file `src/targets/<id>/import-mappers.ts`. Never let `index.ts` import mappers from `importer.ts` and `importer.ts` import the descriptor from `index.ts` — the object literal will capture `undefined` for `map:` fields and silently break import. Create `import-mappers.ts` even when there is only one mapper.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-10.rule: When a target's `rewriteGeneratedPath` or layout references a constant (e.g. `CURSOR_COMPAT_AGENTS`), re-audit the `index.ts` import list at edit time. Treat missing-symbol `ReferenceError` from CLI generate as a release gate, not a runtime curiosity.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-11.rule: Single-letter URI scheme regexes (`^[a-z]+:`) must be kept distinct from Windows drive-letter detection (`^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]`). A scheme matcher that swallows `C:` will block legitimate Windows absolute paths from rewriting. Add regression tests covering both shapes in the same file.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-12.rule: In `resolveGen` and similar dispatchers with a plugin-registry fallback, check `getBuiltinTargetDefinition(target)` FIRST and delegate to `resolveTargetFeatureGenerator(target, feature, config)` for builtins; otherwise the plugin fallback re-applies the raw generator and bypasses conversion config (e.g. `commandsToSkills: false`). Do not let a generic descriptor lookup serve as the builtin path.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-13.rule: Never write a literal `*/` inside any `/* ... */` block comment (including JSDoc and file-header blocks). Replace `skills/*/SKILL.md`-style globs in prose with `skills/{name}/SKILL.md` or move them to single-line `//` comments. The same hazard breaks both production sources and test files.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-14.rule: When a command-orchestration test mocks `loadScopedConfig`, the mocked `ValidatedConfig` must include every field the schema defaults populate (e.g. `plugins: []`). Adding an orchestration step that reads `config.X` without updating every `mockLoadScopedConfig.mockResolvedValue` fixture crashes on `undefined`.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-15.rule: Do not mix CommonJS `require(...)` with top-level `await` in inline `node -e` / heredoc scripts under modern Node — it triggers `ERR_AMBIGUOUS_MODULE_SYNTAX`. Use ESM `import`, or wrap CJS in an async IIFE.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-2.rule: When auto-generating module-level data (e.g. `BUILTIN_TARGETS`) from per-target descriptor imports, patch the existing source file in place between sentinel comments `// <auto-generated:...>` ... `// </auto-generated:...>`. Do NOT extract the array literal to a new generated module — array literals evaluate eagerly and indirection through a separate file adds one more cycle hop that snapshots TDZ-pending imports as `undefined`.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-3.rule: Any lazy registry cache built over `BUILTIN_TARGETS` (or another descriptor-derived list whose own callbacks can trigger the cache during module init) MUST detect TDZ holes (`BUILTIN_TARGETS.filter((d) => d !== undefined)`) and refuse to cache until every slot is populated. "Lazy = safe from cycles" is false; lazy caches that capture mid-init state are worse than no cache.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-4.rule: Whenever a core type becomes a union (e.g. `McpServer` gaining a URL-transport variant), add explicit type guards at every serializer/generator boundary that requires a specific variant, and rerun `pnpm typecheck` before declaring the refactor done.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-5.rule: Read regex capture groups under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` only after narrowing the capture itself: `match?.[1] !== undefined` (or store the value first). Do not rely on regex structure to "guarantee" a capture; the type system does not.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-6.rule: Use explicit strict null comparisons (`!== null` / `!== undefined`). Do not use `!= null` shorthand — the repo lint gate rejects it.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-7.rule: Import Node platform globals (`URL`, `tmpdir`, etc.) explicitly from their `node:` modules. `URL` comes from `node:url`; `tmpdir` from `node:os` (NOT `node:path`); `join`/`resolve` from `node:path`. Ambient Node globals are not implicit under this ESLint config.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-8.rule: After any refactor that touches branch conditions, destructuring, helper extraction, or parsing/normalization control flow, immediately rerun `pnpm lint` AND `pnpm typecheck` — do not defer to broader verification. Sweep dead guard variables that fed the old condition; split destructured returns into `const` for immutable values and a separate `let` only for the one value that is actually reassigned.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-9.rule: When extracting helpers, scan the remaining file for every symbol that moved and run the narrowest affected test suite immediately — do not assume "mechanical split" is safe. A preservation branch left over with a removed import surfaces as `ReferenceError` only at runtime.

verification-workflow-changing-the-publi.rule: Changing the public API surface (adding, removing, or renaming exports under src/public/*.ts) must be mirrored in the consumer-smoke fixture tests/consumer-smoke/src/smoke.ts, which compiles against the PACKED TARBALL under strict tsc as a separate release gate (pnpm consumer-smoke) that the normal vitest suite never runs; a stale fixture surfaces only at build/pack time with TS2305/TS2724 missing-export errors.

verification-workflow-do-not-run-dist-de.rule: Do not run dist-dependent E2E tests concurrently with a build or full test command that cleans and recreates dist; build first, then run those E2E tests serially to avoid false MODULE_NOT_FOUND failures.

verification-workflow-in-this-dogfooding.rule: In this dogfooding repo, most generated target dirs (.aider, .cursor, .cline, .github/{instructions,prompts,agents,skills}, .gemini, …) and several root agent files are GITIGNORED, regenerable functional state — NOT cruft. A 'remove unneeded files' request must NOT delete them (deleting breaks 'generate --check' and the dogfood; rerun 'agentsmesh generate' to restore). Genuine cruft = stale agentsmesh-*.tgz, coverage/, dist/ (rebuildable), .DS_Store, and .agentsmesh/lessons/*-log.jsonl telemetry. Verify each target is git-ignored AND non-source before rm.

verification-workflow-pnpm-precommit-the.rule: pnpm precommit (the husky pre-commit hook) runs typecheck + lint:dead (knip) + test:coverage (full suite, 95% gate) + lint-staged — a heavy ~3min gate that can flake on a single run (watch/timing or coverage). If a commit fails on the pre-commit hook, re-run 'pnpm precommit' standalone before treating it as a real regression; for non-.ts-only commits whose gate you just verified green, --no-verify is justified to avoid a redundant full-suite rerun.

verification-workflow-run-package-surfac.rule: Run package-surface analyzers such as attw only after the build finishes; running them concurrently with a dist-cleaning build can falsely report missing types.

verification-workflow-tests-e2e-agents-l.rule: tests/e2e/agents-last-run.md is a git-TRACKED report that the agents e2e suite rewrites with a fresh _Generated: <timestamp>_ on every run, so it shows as modified after any full or e2e test run. Revert it (git checkout --) before staging a release commit so the timestamp churn never lands; better, it should be gitignored or written to a temp path.

verification-workflow-tests-e2e-agents-l.rationale: The file was gitignored to stop timestamp dirty-tree churn; the old lesson assuming it is git-tracked is now wrong.
verification-workflow-tests-e2e-agents-l.rule: tests/e2e/agents-last-run.md is gitignored (added to .gitignore, untracked via `git rm --cached`); the agents e2e suite still rewrites it on disk each run for inspection but it is no longer committed. Do NOT re-track or commit it, and do NOT use `git checkout --` to "restore" it. Any test-written diagnostic report carrying a fresh `_Generated: <timestamp>_` line must stay gitignored (or write to a temp path) — never a committed fixture — so e2e/full test runs leave the working tree clean.

verification-workflow-tests-for-env-gate.rule: Tests for env-gated features must explicitly set or clear the relevant environment variable instead of assuming the developer environment default.
Tests for env-gated features must explicitly set or clear the relevant environment variable instead of assuming the developer environment default.

verification-workflow-the-coverage-gate-.rule: The coverage gate is GLOBAL (vitest.config thresholds over the included set), not per-file. v8 counts the right-hand operand of defensive `?? fallback` / `=== undefined` guards on regex match groups (forced by noUncheckedIndexedAccess: match.index, match[n], match.indices[n]) as branches that are UNREACHABLE at runtime. When raising branch coverage, cover the reachable logic and rely on the global threshold — do NOT add ! non-null assertions (lint-forbidden), v8-ignore comments (the repo uses none), or contrived tests to juice an individual file's branch %.

verification-workflow-the-husky-pre-comm.rule: The husky pre-commit hook runs pnpm test:coverage, which includes git-touching tests (remote-fetcher-git, lessons-merge-driver, refresh-drift-flow, refresh-git-source, install-script's 'git ls-files --stage'). Run inside 'git commit', they collide with the commit's .git/index.lock and fail spuriously ('Unable to create .git/*.lock', empty git ls-files output, merge-driver missing a rule) yet pass standalone. When a commit's only failures are these git-contention artifacts and the change is independently verified (full suite green standalone), commit with --no-verify.

verification-workflow-verify-a-reference.rule: Verify a referenced source path exists before reading it during review; use rg --files or the actual import path instead of assuming an application.ts module name.

verification-workflow-when-locating-a-gl.rule: When locating a globally installed CLI, use command -v plus npm root -g first; do not make pnpm root -g part of a chained probe because an unconfigured pnpm global bin can fail the whole command.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-1.rule: In tests, import `runWatch` from `tests/harness/watch.js` — never from `src/cli/commands/watch.js` directly; mock the production module path separately while keeping the harness import.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-10.rule: When a watch test needs to wait for "the next regen cycle", thread an `onCycle({ featuresChanged })` callback into `runWatch` and assert on `cycles.length`/`cycles[i].featuresChanged` — never scrape `infoSpy.toHaveBeenCalledWith('Regenerated.')` or other externally-observable log/spy side-effects (the startup generate already fires them, producing tautological waits). Keep `scripts/flake-check-watch.ts` (N=10 under `COVERAGE=1`) and `pnpm flake:watch` wired in `package.json` to validate stability whenever the watch loop changes.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-11.rule: Any test that creates a watch then writes into a just-created subdirectory must force chokidar's polling backend (`usePolling: true, interval: 50`) via `tests/harness/watch.ts` rather than rely on native `fs.watch` — macOS FSEvents and Linux inotify drop events on freshly-added subtrees under parallel scheduler load. Keep production native for real interactive use; never trust kernel event delivery in parallel test environments.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-12.rule: Keep e2e CLI helper timeouts (e.g. `runCli` 30s) high enough for full-suite parallel pressure; reproduce timeout-looking failures both targeted and under the full runner before treating them as product behavior failures.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-2.rule: Watch tests that mutate files after `runWatch()` must first wait for an initial generated artifact or log signal, then perform the edit and wait for the expected reaction — never assume the watcher is past its initial generation/readiness phase under full-suite scheduler load.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-3.rule: `runWatch()` must wait for the chokidar `ready` event before doing the initial reconciliation/generate; verify both the isolated watch suite and full `pnpm test` after any watcher-startup change.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-4.rule: Watch-mode ignore filters must suppress both exact generated files (e.g. `.agentsmesh/.lock`, `.agentsmesh/.lock.tmp`) AND the canonical parent directory event emitted when those bookkeeping files churn; validate with the isolated watch suite and the full `pnpm test` run.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-5.rule: After bumping any test-runner or watcher-adjacent dependency (e.g. Vitest 4.0.x → 4.1.x), rerun the full suite and increase watch-unit `vi.waitFor` budgets again if needed — isolated green runs are not enough.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-6.rule: Keep watch unit `vi.waitFor` timeouts comfortably above 3000 ms (for example 8000 ms) and idle-stability delays at least 3000 ms — `pnpm test:coverage` slows chokidar debounce + generate past short budgets even when plain `pnpm test` is green.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-7.rule: Any watcher test must create a fresh temp project directory per test case; never reuse a prior watched path after teardown — shared temp dirs leak chokidar state under coverage load.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-8.rule: Never run test commands in parallel when they touch the same temp paths, ports, caches, or repo artifacts (e.g. fixed `ab-watch-cmd-test`).

watch-and-test-timing-rule-9.rule: Watch tests that prove event-driven behavior must keep the watcher in a `finally` cleanup and retry the triggering write until the observed callback fires or the normal timeout expires — chokidar may miss a lone create event under full-suite saturation.

website-docs-in-website-docs-pages-under.rationale: Existing quick-start.mdx links like ../guides/installing-skill-packs/ resolve to /getting-started/guides/... (404); copying that convention propagates the bug.
website-docs-in-website-docs-pages-under.rule: In website docs pages under a nested directory (e.g. getting-started/), link to sibling sections with ../../<section>/ not ../<section>/ — Starlight serves pages at /section/page/ with a trailing slash, so ../ resolves inside the page's own directory and the link 404s. Verify by resolving the raw href against the page URL.

website-docs-in-website-keep-every-depen.rationale: website/pnpm-lock.yaml is not committed, so fresh installs re-resolve ranges; the root repo ships zod 4 which leaks into the website build via Node resolution walk-up.
website-docs-in-website-keep-every-depen.rule: In website/, keep every dependency on a zod-3-compatible version (zod devDep is pinned to ^3.25.76 to satisfy stray bare `zod` imports that otherwise walk up to the repo root's zod 4 and crash Astro's content layer). Before adding a Starlight plugin, check its zod major: a zod-4 plugin (e.g. starlight-links-validator >= 0.15) fails with `.prefault is not a function`; pin the last zod-3 release instead.

website-docs-when-applying-a-readability.rationale: A readability audit flagged 10 pages; on inspection 9 already had clear leads and good structure, so editing on the audit's say-so would have degraded good docs.
website-docs-when-applying-a-readability.rule: When applying a readability/quality audit to website docs, verify each of the audit subagent's specific claims against the real file before editing — survey agents over-flag (e.g. claim a page "has no lead" when it opens with one, mis-count lines, or call distinct sections "duplicated"). Don't churn already-good pages; only edit where the real file genuinely needs it. Verify doc edits with `npx astro build` in `website/` (~6s; it builds all pages and validates every internal link).

windows-paths-a-directory-rename-that-fi.rule: A directory rename that finalizes a cache slot right after a child process wrote the tree (e.g. git clone then rename staging->final in git-remote.ts) can throw EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY on Windows because the exited writer handle, an antivirus scan, or the search indexer still pins the fresh files; wrap such post-subprocess directory renames in a bounded retry on transient codes (renameWithRetry) rather than surfacing a spurious fetch failure.

windows-paths-an-ancestor-walk-that-dete.rule: An ancestor-walk that detects an agentsmesh project by a bare '.agentsmesh' dir false-positives on the global-mode config at ~/.agentsmesh (which '--lessons' never populates). Key the detection off the actual artifact (.agentsmesh/lessons/lessons.json), not the bare dir. Also: unit tests that mkdtemp under tmpdir() and walk UP are contaminated on Windows CI runners where ~/.agentsmesh exists (tmpdir is under the home dir, unlike macOS /var/folders or Linux /tmp) — assert against the precise artifact, never a bare .agentsmesh.

windows-paths-integration-tests-that-dri.rule: Integration tests that drive a real git clone+checkout of a local bare repo (e.g. tests/integration/refresh-git-source) flake on Windows CI with a spurious 'not a git repository' at checkout — the freshly-cloned .git is momentarily invisible to the next git process (the AV/indexer/handle-release timing renameWithRetry already guards in git-remote.ts). Guard the suite with vitest describe(name, { retry: 2 }, fn): a retry re-runs beforeEach with a fresh clone and absorbs the environmental flake, while a deterministic refresh-logic regression still fails every attempt. Prefer retry over it.skipIf(win32) so Windows coverage is kept.

windows-paths-on-windows-only-a-git.rule: On Windows only, a git merge-driver command (or any git-config value git executes via sh) that embeds an absolute CLI path with backslashes fails because sh consumes the backslashes (D:\a\...\dist\cli.js collapses to D:adistcli.js -> MODULE_NOT_FOUND), so the driver exits non-zero and git reports a spurious merge conflict; normalize the path to forward slashes (replaceAll backslash to slash) before embedding it, since Node accepts forward slashes on Windows.

windows-paths-rule-1.rule: **Never `split('/')` a filesystem path.** Use `basename(path[, ext])` from `node:path`. On Windows, `path.join` produces `\` separators, so `split('/').pop()` returns the *entire* path and downstream `mkdir` blows up on `C:/...` segments. Audit `split('/').pop()`, `split('/').slice(-N)`, and `endsWith('/x')` against native path fields whenever new path-derived identifiers land.

windows-paths-rule-10.rule: **Strip Windows absolute path tokens before "no canonical path in output" assertions.** The link rebaser intentionally leaves Windows absolutes untouched (`WINDOWS_ABSOLUTE_PATH` guard), so legitimate `\.agentsmesh\` substrings inside `C:\...\.agentsmesh\rules\typescript.md` trip naive `not.toContain('.agentsmesh\\')` checks. Extend `stripProtectedRegions` (or local assertion helpers) to drop `/[A-Za-z]:[\\/][^\s,<>"'`+`'`'`+`]+/g` first.

windows-paths-rule-11.rule: **Skip-on-Windows is the correct answer for POSIX-only test contracts.** Tests that (a) construct canonical content with absolute paths that turn into `C:\...` on Windows, (b) stub `git` via chmod-755 Node scripts, (c) pass `NODE_OPTIONS=--import=<windows path>`, or (d) assert POSIX mode bits (`statSync(p).mode & 0o111`) must `it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')`. For mode bits, query the git index (`git ls-files --stage`) instead — NTFS doesn't surface execute bits.

windows-paths-rule-12.rule: **Walkers across project trees must skip `.agentsmesh`, `.agentsmeshcache`, `node_modules`, `.git` at directory-entry level AND wrap `readdirSync`/`statSync` in try/catch.** Windows TOCTOU between exiting CLI processes and test walkers ENOENTs mid-walk; the cache dir vanishes between readdir and stat.

windows-paths-rule-13.rule: **Bound symlink-based temp-project setups to dot-entries and root files only.** `createTempProjectRoot(homedir())` must never indiscriminately symlink Desktop/Documents/Downloads — `listScopedAgentsFiles` will recurse into them. Symlink only dot-directories (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, ...) and root-level files. The same scope guard applies to `global` import: never run whole-tree `readDirRecursive(homedir())` for nested rule discovery; restrict to `~/.codex`, `~/.agents/skills`, etc.

windows-paths-rule-14.rule: **Cross-platform path fixtures must resolve in the real file tree.** Don't translate POSIX `../SKILL.md` to `..\\SKILL.md` without rechecking the file's actual directory layout — sibling references must exist in both shapes.

windows-paths-rule-15.rule: **`tmpdir` is from `node:os`, not `node:path`.** Stop the copy-paste before it lands.

windows-paths-rule-16.rule: **For inline-backtick path rewrites and any assertion that depends on realpath equivalence, accept multiple equivalent forms.** DOS 8.3 short names (`RUNNER~1` → `runneradmin`) make `expandResolvedPaths` and `toProjectRootRelative` non-deterministic on Windows tmp dirs. Use permissive regexes like `` /`(?:\.{1,2}\/)*\/?docs\/some-doc\.md`/ `` — the contract is "reaches a stable destination," not "always rewrites to project-root-relative."

windows-paths-rule-17.rule: **Tests that need merged stdout+stderr must not hardcode a POSIX shell.** Use `spawnSync(process.execPath, [...args], { encoding: 'utf-8' })` and concatenate `result.stdout + result.stderr`. Never embed `2>&1` or hardcode `/bin/sh` / `/bin/zsh` once Windows is in the CI matrix.

windows-paths-rule-18.rule: **Control-character escapes in regex literals must survive the `Write` JSON transport.** Build via `new RegExp('[<>:"|?*\\u0000-\\u001F]')` so the file stores literal escape sequences, not raw bytes. Verify with `file(1)` after authoring.

windows-paths-rule-19.rule: **Project-relative path validators must reject Windows absolutes independently of host OS.** Native `path.isAbsolute()` does not recognize `C:\...` as absolute on POSIX, so cross-platform canonical path validators must also reject `/^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/` before resolving against a project root.

windows-paths-rule-2.rule: **Pick `node:path` vs `node:path/posix` by path *format*, not host platform.** Any code in `src/core/reference/` or `applyXxxRefs` helpers that participates in the link-rewrite map (key construction OR lookup) MUST use `pathApi(projectRoot)` from `src/core/path-helpers.ts`. Never import `join`/`normalize` from `node:path` directly there. In synthetic-root unit tests (`ROOT = '/proj'`), alias `join`/`normalize` to `posix.join`/`posix.normalize`.

windows-paths-rule-3.rule: **Test helpers that fake `$HOME` must set `USERPROFILE` on win32.** `node:os.homedir()` reads `USERPROFILE` (not `HOME`) on Windows. Centralize the translation in the spawn helper, not at every call site.

windows-paths-rule-4.rule: **Normalize native-path test assertions through `toPosixPath()`.** `fromPath`, `srcPath`, and similar fields are intentionally native (callers pass them to `fs.readFileSync`); rewrite the *assertion*, not the production code. Use `tests/helpers/posix-path.ts` for `.toContain('.codex/...')` / `.includes('...')` checks.

windows-paths-rule-5.rule: **CLI display paths must be `.replaceAll('\\', '/')` before printing.** Tests assert forward slashes unconditionally; native `node:path` separators leak platform differences into user-facing output.

windows-paths-rule-6.rule: **Chokidar must use `usePolling: process.platform === 'win32'` in production, and force polling in *every* watch test on every OS.** Windows tmp dirs under `AppData\Local\Temp\...` miss `ReadDirectoryChangesW` events on freshly-created subdirs; macOS FSEvents + Linux inotify drop events under parallel suite load on just-mkdir'd subtrees. Wrap `runWatch` via `tests/harness/watch.ts` and always pass `{ usePolling: true, interval: 50 }`.

windows-paths-rule-7.rule: **Prefer the caller's projectRoot-shaped path over realpath; treat realpath as a tie-breaker.** On Windows runners under `RUNNER~1`, `realpathSync.native` expands to the long form (`runneradmin`), and `toProjectRootRelative(short, long)` yields `..\..\..` chains. In `expandResolvedPaths` and any `[realpath, original]` loop, the caller-shaped variant must win.

windows-paths-rule-8.rule: **Cross-platform repos commit `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf` and explicit text categories.** Don't rely on per-runner git config — Windows runners default `core.autocrlf=true`, rewriting fixture `.md`/`.json`/`.yaml` to CRLF on checkout while `writeFileAtomic` emits LF. For tests that stage repo files into a tmpdir, use `writeFileSync(to, readFileSync(from, 'utf-8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n'))` instead of `copyFileSync`.

windows-paths-rule-9.rule: **URI/scheme detection must not swallow Windows drive letters.** Keep the URI scheme matcher distinct from `[A-Za-z]:[\\/]` drive-letter detection. Plugin/source `isLocalSource` classifiers must accept `D:\foo` alongside POSIX absolutes — `node:path`'s `resolve()` produces drive-letter absolutes on win32. Regression tests cover both `C:` and `ssh://...` in the same file.
